The branch pre-activates configured heartbeat channel plugins at gateway startup, adds an `allowBundledFallback` resolver option, disables heartbeat wake-path bootstrap/bundled fallback, and updates outbound heartbeat tests.

PR surface: Source +89, Tests +94. Total +183 across 6 files.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): skip plugin bootstrap and bundled fallback during delivery target resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a heartbeat wake-loop latency regression where delivery-target resolution blocks for ~60s per tick when the configured channel plugin is not already in the active runtime registry.

### Background

Commit [`6470bb7625`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6470bb7625) (fix(heartbeat): bootstrap plugin session targets, #93630) solved a real problem: when a user configured `heartbeat.target` to a channel id that was not in the built-in known-deliverable-channel list (e.g. a third-party plugin id), `normalizeDeliverableOutboundChannel()` returned `undefined` and the target was silently dropped to `"none"`.

The fix called `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` in the heartbeat delivery-target path. However, this triggers `resolveRuntimePluginRegistry()` → `loadOpenClawPlugins()`, which scans **all** installed plugins — not just the target channel.

### Root cause analysis

The `bootstrapOutboundChannelPlugin` guard in `channel-bootstrap.runtime.ts` has a `bootstrapAttempts` Set that caches per `(registryVersion, channel)` key:
- **Successful bootstrap**: key stays cached → subsequent ticks skip instantly
- **Failed bootstrap** (plugin not installed / config issue / transient failure): key is deleted → every tick re-runs the full plugin scan

This is the pathological case: a misconfigured or not-yet-installed heartbeat plugin channel causes repeated ~60s scans on every wake tick.

### When this bug is triggered

1. `heartbeat.target` is not `"none"` or `"last"`
2. The target channel is not in the active runtime registry
3. `heartbeat.to` is set (non-empty)

## Why This Change Was Made

Three-part fix:

### Part 1: Hot path optimization

Three heartbeat-path call sites in `targets.ts` now pass `allowBootstrap: false, allowBundledFallback: false`. A new `allowBundledFallback` parameter is added to `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin` (default `true`) so hot paths can skip both the bootstrap scan AND the `getBundledChannelPlugin` lazy-load fallback.

### Part 2: Startup pre-activation

A new `preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins()` function in `src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.ts` runs **once at gateway startup** (in `activateGatewayScheduledServices`, before `startHeartbeatRunner`). It reads the heartbeat config, finds every effective non-standard channel target, and calls `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin({ allowBootstrap: true })` to load the plugin into the active registry before the wake loop starts.

This preserves the delivery compatibility that PR #93630 established — external plugin channel heartbeat targets still get bootstrapped — but moves the bootstrap cost from the hot path (every tick) to startup (once).

### Part 3: Per-agent heartbeat coverage (rev 2)

The pre-activation function iterates both `agents.defaults.heartbeat` AND `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries, merging per-agent overrides over defaults (matching `resolveHeartbeatConfig` in the runner). This ensures per-agent external plugin heartbeat targets — which the runner schedules independently of the default — are also pre-activated before the wake loop starts.

Standard deliverable channels (telegram, discord, etc.) and targets of `"none"`/`"last"` are no-ops in pre-activation.

## User Impact

- **Normal deployment (plugin active)**: No change — plugin found in registry, <10ms resolution both before and after
- **Plugin not yet active** (external channel, delayed activation, per-agent override): Pre-activation resolves it at startup (~135–739ms once) instead of every heartbeat tick (~60s each). All effective heartbeat configs (default + per-agent) are covered.
- **Plugin not installed / misconfigured**: Fast fail at startup (best-effort bootstrap) and fast fail on hot path — no repeated scans

## Compatibility

- `allowBundledFallback` defaults to `true` — all non-heartbeat callers unchanged
- Pre-activation is a no-op for standard channel targets and `target: none/last`
- Pre-activation covers per-agent `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries with the same merge semantics as `resolveHeartbeatConfig` in the runner
- `resolveOutboundTarget` (general-purpose outbound) continues to pass `params.allowBootstrap` through transparently

## Evidence

### Unit tests (96/96 passed)

```
src/infra/outbound/targets.test.ts                  85 passed
src/infra/outbound/heartbeat-pre-activate.test.ts   11 passed
```

New tests cover: per-agent external plugin target without default heartbeat, per-agent target overriding default, entries without heartbeat blocks skipped, target deduplication across agents.

### Probe timing (isolated vitest)

```
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):  739ms (external-channel, once at startup)
Pre-activation bootstrap (cold scan):  135ms (plugin-channel, once at startup)
Hot path (allowBootstrap: false):       <10ms (registry lookup, every tick)
```

### Lint / type / format checks

```
oxlint:    clean
tsgo:      clean (check:test-types)
format:    clean (oxfmt --check)
build:     clean (pnpm build)
```

### Review response

- **Rev 1 review**: Added startup pre-activation (`preactivateHeartbeatChannelPlugins`) to preserve delivery compatibility lost by removing bootstrap from the hot path. ([clawsweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100377#issuecomment-4886719486))
- **Rev 2 review**: Extended pre-activation to iterate `agents.list[].heartbeat` entries so per-agent external plugin heartbeat targets are also covered — matches the effective configs `resolveHeartbeatAgents` schedules. ([clawsweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100377#issuecomment-4886719486))
